minor.comment: Every Dispatcher-addressed delivery now names the Dispatcher Command instead of omitting a Team name: an unbound conversation, the single fallback after a bound Team proved it admitted nothing, and a document-comment cold open invoke `dispatcher.submit`, and `/stop` in an unbound conversation invokes `dispatcher.interrupt`. A Collaboration Space message whose Team could not be provisioned is no longer delivered to the Dispatcher Agent: the Channel replies under the triggering message with `Could not start a Team for this conversation. The reason is in the Dreamux log.` and submits nothing. The notice carries no reason because raw failure text can name host state paths; the reason stays on the delivery log line, which is unchanged. `failed`, `ambiguous`, and `error` are logged with no notice as before, and a settled question-card answer whose topic plans provisioning is dropped with its log line rather than notified or re-routed.

The `reply` tool now takes exactly `chat_id`, optional `message_id`, and `text`; the `mention_user_ids` argument is gone, and a mention is written in the body with Feishu's own `<at user_id="ou_example">Example</at>` syntax, which the tool description now shows. Replies are still delivered as Markdown cards, now one Markdown element per card: a leading heading is no longer lifted into the card title and a table is no longer a native table element. A Team the channel provisions automatically for a Collaboration Space topic is now created with the space's configured identity followed by its bound reply address — the chat and the message that triggered creation — so the leader can still address the conversation after a compaction; the space policy is unchanged. A failed send now reports the platform's own status, code, reason, and log id in the channel log and the MCP failure.

Refuse to bind the whole chat a Collaboration Space is registered on. A group row on a Space's container answered routing for every topic under it, so the Space silently stopped giving new topics their own Team. bind_channel and /bind are both refused now; a topic inside the Space is still bindable, which is what provisioning installs.

An `ask_user_question` card now stays answerable for 24 hours instead of 14 minutes. The tool gains an optional `text` argument: Markdown, including `<at user_id="ou_example">Example</at>` mentions, shown above the questions so one card can carry the explanation and the decision. The explanation remains on submitted, cancelled, and expired cards. The answer delivered to the model does not repeat it.

Three new MCP tools let a caller follow one Feishu document's comments: `subscribe_document`, `unsubscribe_document`, and `list_subscriptions`. Each is offered to both the Dispatcher and a TeamLeader with no recipient argument — the caller is the recipient — so a caller can only create, list, and remove its own rows. Subscribing takes a document URL or a token plus its `type`, resolves a wiki URL to the document the node holds, and refuses when Feishu proves this bot cannot see the document. Subscriptions live in a third `subscriptions` section of the channel's existing routing document, which stays readable as it is: a file written before this release reads the section as empty. A received comment event produces one submission per subscriber, in the same envelope an inbound chat message uses: the facts that address the comment are attributes on it, and its body is the `<content>` the commenter wrote — with a mention rendered as the same `<at user_id="…">` element a chat mention becomes — beside a `<quote>` holding the document text the comment is anchored to. The comment is read once per delivered event and its absence never costs the event. A comment nobody subscribed to reaches the Dispatcher Agent when it @-mentions the bot and the commenter is already one of the dispatcher's trusted users, and is dropped and logged otherwise; that delivery creates no subscription. A subscriber whose Team is closed or gone loses its own subscription and no one else's, and dissolving a Team drops its subscriptions alongside its bindings. Feishu delivers these events on the bot's own notification rule: a document written under this bot's identity delivers every comment on it, while on a document someone else wrote only a comment that @-mentions this bot or a reply in a thread this bot has already replied in arrives. Subscribing widens none of that; the subscribe tool's description states the rule so a caller can decide who should write a document in the first place.

A delivered document comment now says what it is about. Three attributes join the envelope: `anchor`, which is `whole_document` or `content` and is absent exactly when the comment could not be read — so a comment the commenter put on the whole document is no longer indistinguishable from one with no text; `anchor_id`, Feishu's id for the anchored content, which for a docx is the block id lark-cli reads back in full; and `anchor_deleted`, written only when Feishu says the anchored content is gone. The `<quote>` block is unchanged in shape but no longer described as the document text the comment is anchored to: its note now says it is a preview Feishu shortens, and points at `anchor_id` for the content itself. The channel fetches no anchored content of its own — one anchored part can be far larger than every comment on it, and the recipient decides whether it wants the passage. A delivered comment is also logged for what it was. The log said "delivered" for every outcome but a proven rejection, which hid a comment refused because the session had closed and a body Core would not admit; it now reports what Core answered — admitted, not admitted, rejected before admission, ambiguous, or failed — at the severity each earns. Both delivery paths read that classification from one place beside the outcome type instead of each keeping its own, because they had already drifted apart on it; each keeps only its own wording. The chat path's log lines are unchanged except that its failure lines now also carry the outcome's `status`.

Add Feishu /bind and /help commands with yargs-parser arguments. Bind the whole chat, announce in the requesting conversation without moving a Team anchor across targets, and show Previous Team when rebinding.

`list_bindings` now accepts four optional filters — `team_name`, `chat_id`, `thread_id`, and `target_kind` (`group` or `topic`) — matched exactly and combined with AND, so the Dispatcher can ask for one Team's routes or one chat's rows instead of reading the whole table. `target_kind` is the only way to ask for whole-chat bindings alone, and it offers no `p2p` because a Feishu direct chat cannot be bound to a Team; a value outside the two is refused naming both. Calling the tool with no arguments still returns every binding, matching nothing is an ordinary empty answer, and the result shape is unchanged.

Every Feishu send resolves its destination through one path: `reply`, `ask_user_question`, extension cards and system notices. An explicit message address is used as is; in a Collaboration Space chat a send that names no message lands in the caller's bound topic and is refused when the caller does not have exactly one bound topic with a known root message. A binding whose topic root message is unknown (a manual bind, or a topic bound by an earlier build) learns it from the next inbound message in that topic, or by reading the topic's messages, so bind, unbind and dissolve notices reach the topic instead of being dropped. When Feishu auto-provisions a Team, the leader's identity carries the initial chat id and topic root message id. The first CoT card after a manual bind anchors to the binding notice that was sent, when no anchor exists yet. Card clicks (ask-user select, input, submit and cancel, and extension card actions) now pass the same access policy as inbound messages before any side effect: only a person the conversation's inbound policy admits may answer. The click event carries no chat kind, so the policy is applied for both a direct chat and a group, and the kind is established only when the two decisions differ: the kind comes from the chat itself, never from the access lists: the kind reported by an admitted inbound message this session already routed in that chat, else a Feishu lookup; and a click that still depends on that answer and cannot get it is refused, which needs the group information read permission that topic collaboration already asks for, such as `im:chat:readonly`. Ask-user answers are therefore narrower than before, when any member of the chat could answer.

The named createFeishuPlugin factory contributes the feishu channel provider and publishes its extension API for other plugins. The package-root default remains a neutral provider factory for npm:@excitedjs/feishu-channel; createFeishuChannelProvider is unchanged. Existing provider configuration continues to load.

Inbound messages reach the model as one `` body. A mention is written `Name`, the same syntax the `reply` tool takes, for every message type and only where the platform's mention records name one; a record without a user identity reads as `@Name`. A card is read from the event alone, contributes its text and its images and files, and gets a `` row saying it is a rich card the model can pull in full with lark-cli; the two card reads and their merge are gone. Images and files anywhere in a message are downloaded, cached, and budgeted as before and rendered as `` where they stood. Code blocks are fenced Markdown instead of ``. `FeishuInboundEvent` carries `text` and `resources` instead of `parsedText` and `contentParts`; `FEISHU_SKILL_FALLBACK_NOTE` is removed.

Code organization refactor stage 8b (Feishu directory reorganization): (1) R37 - every card the package builds is now Card JSON 2.0 (schema '2.0', elements under body.elements); the pairing approval button uses a direct Card 2.0 callback button; the binding-bound/unbound/team-dissolved notification cards go through the shared card kit, which now takes an explicit forward flag so those three cards keep their prior forwardable behavior unchanged; no other visible text, layout, button, or export name changed. (2) R38 - bind_space/get_space/list_spaces no longer report a generation field and list_bindings no longer reports an origin field, since neither was read by any code, only surfaced verbatim. (3) R38/R41 - a topic-kind binding now persists the message id that first triggered it (root_message_id) when automatic provisioning installed it; a manual bind never sets it but preserves one already on the row. (4) R41 - every outbound send now reads the chat/topic it actually landed in off Feishu's own send response instead of a session-local recent-message guess, fixing a class of reply-lands-in-the-wrong-topic bug once two conversations interleave; a reply with no message_id inside a Collaboration Space chat is refused with an instruction, or redirected to the caller's own bound topic when it has exactly one, instead of silently opening a new topic, for every caller kind; a newly auto-provisioned leader's identity preserves the configured identity and appends the bound chat id, the message id that triggered creation, and guidance to use the current message id or that initial id when replying. (5) Ask-user rounds now read their card's landing off the send response the same way. Card-action dispatch (extension keys, pairing approval, the four ask_user_* actions) resolves through one shared action table instead of two separate hardcoded checks. (6) The nine-file feishu-cot-*.ts layout and feishu-inbound-anchor.ts regroup under cot/ by responsibility - the state machine (adapter.ts), byte-size math (bytes.ts), card-event building (card.ts), recipient/anchor state (recipients.ts), the diagnostic log shape (diagnostics.ts), bounded platform I/O (io.ts), and which in-flight submissions are this session's own (inbound-correlations.ts); no behavior or persisted-format change. (7) feishu-channel.ts and feishu-session-ops.ts fold into session/session.ts, replacing the free-function SessionHandle bag with named collaborators or private methods; a built-in MCP tool call now gets the same post-teardown liveness fence an extension tool call already had. FeishuTeamSubmitter is no longer exported (single-method interface with one call site, replaced by a plain function type). Card-click answering and card-driven delivery (an extension's forward, an ask-user settlement, the pairing-approval click) move to a new session/card-actions.ts collaborator the session constructs and delegates to, rather than living as six more private methods on the session class itself. (8) The session, inbound, outbound, access, ask-user, chain-of-thought, and card files move under directories named for what they own (session/, inbound/, outbound/, access/, ask-user/, cot/, cards/); routing/ and tools/ already existed. Files with a single already-clear owner (feishu-submit.ts, feishu-provisioning.ts, feishu-extensions.ts, feishu-slash-commands.ts, feishu-document-comments.ts, bot.ts, extension.ts, plugin.ts, provider.ts, and others) stay at the package root. No behavior change from the moves themselves. (9) The package's public surface (index.ts, the sole package.json exports target) shrinks to the named plugin entry createFeishuPlugin, plus the compatible default/createFeishuChannelProvider neutral provider entry (without plugin extensions), the full extension contract an implementing plugin needs (FeishuApi/FeishuExtension*/FeishuInstanceApi plus their own transitive types - FeishuCardActionEvent, FeishuCardActionResponse/rawCardActionResponse, FeishuTarget, FeishuToolResult, DREAMUX_ACTION_KEY), and the two names packages/dreamux's own test suite reads as a cross-package consumer (formatFeishuMessageForRuntime, FeishuInboundEvent). Every other name the barrel re-exported previously (FeishuChannelSession and its session types, createFeishuSessionMcp, CHANNEL_REMINDER/FeishuChatSubmission/FeishuInboundDelivery/FeishuSubmission/FeishuSubmitOutcome, the FEISHU_TOOLS/FeishuToolContext/FeishuToolDef/FeishuToolSession tool-registry group, FeishuRouting/FeishuBindingView/FeishuRoutingPlan/FeishuRoutingStore/routingDocumentFilename/FEISHU_ROUTING_DOCUMENT_VERSION/FeishuBindingRecord/FeishuRoutingDocument/FeishuSpaceRecord, chatTarget/describeTarget/targetKey/topicTarget/FeishuTargetKind, createFeishuBot/FeishuBot/CreateBotOptions, DREAMUX_PAIRING_CARD_ACTION/DREAMUX_PAIRING_TOKEN_KEY, buildPairingApprovalCard/buildPairingSuccessCard, loadChatBots/PeerBot/ChatBotsListing, formatFeishuCreateTime/FormatFeishuMessageOptions/FormatFeishuMessageResult/FormattedFeishuAttachment, dreamuxFeishuGate, defaultDispatcherAccessState/DispatcherAccessState, VisibleMessageAnchor, and BUILTIN_FEISHU_PROVIDER_REF) had zero consumers reaching it through the package boundary rather than a relative import inside the package, and is removed; every internal caller already used the concrete module. Old routing documents keep loading unchanged under all of this - the generation/origin/root_message_id shape change is additive/stop-writing only. Not BREAKING.

A `channels[].config` block for the built-in Feishu provider now follows the same persisted-shape policy (R21) as the rest of config.json: an unrecognized key alongside `app_id`/`app_secret` is tolerated and ignored instead of refusing `dreamux serve`. A missing or wrong-type `app_id`/`app_secret` still fails loading.

Code organization refactor stage 2b, item 5: enable exactOptionalPropertyTypes. FeishuBot.cot (published from src/index.ts) now types as accepting an explicit undefined, not only omission. Non-breaking widening; no runtime change.

Code organization refactor stage 4a: the routing document, access.json, and chat-bots.json are now each held in memory for the session's life through one shared TransactionalStore primitive (issue #448), replacing the routing store's own write logic, the access mutex, and chat-bots' inline temp-file writer. access.json and chat-bots.json used to be re-read from disk on every operation; a hand edit to either file while the daemon is running is no longer picked up until the daemon restarts (the routing document already worked this way). access.json no longer writes PendingPairingEntry.kind/.replies or the last_gate/observed_chats/warnings ledger fields (old files that still have them keep reading; PendingPairingEntry.created_at is unaffected and still written); the 'warn once per dispatcher run on multi-chat traffic' log event is gone, replaced by chat_id on the existing per-message pair log lines. Public exports changed: TRUST_DOMAIN_WARNING, loadDispatcherAccess, saveDispatcherAccess, and listChatBots are removed, and defaultDispatcherAccessState()'s shape shrank by the three deleted ledger fields.

Code organization refactor stage 6f, item 5 (R50): a Feishu extension's state root now nests under the Feishu plugin's own state directory (ServerHost.stateDir, captured in plugin.ts's server()) plus the dispatcher id, instead of the channel instance's state_root it borrowed before. access.json, chat-bots.json, and the routing document are untouched; this mechanism has not shipped in a release.

Give submission, inbound routing, notifications and question expiry explicit operation owners while preserving provisioning waiters and pairing send-before-save. Remove CreateFeishuChannelProviderOptions and provider/plugin botFactory overrides, plus unused internal transport/clock/id/timer overrides; standalone provider construction remains supported.

The Feishu extension api's `FeishuInstanceApi` has no `submitToTeam`, and `sendCard` takes no `mode` field. A card action handler returns `{ response, forward? }`: `response` answers the card callback, and `forward`, when present, states text to deliver to the conversation's Team — Feishu resolves that Team from the card and delivers it through the same path an ask-user answer takes, so no extension holds Team-resolution or delivery logic of its own.

Refuse to register a collaboration space on a chat already bound as a whole to a Team. A whole-chat binding answers routing for every topic under it, so the space would never provision a Team for a new topic and nothing would report it. This is the same invariant bind_channel already enforces from the other side; binding a single topic is unaffected. A document written before this rule that already holds both keeps loading and routing exactly as it did; re-registering that space refuses until the whole-chat binding is released, which is also the repair.
Revert #408 and restore the previous workspace and Team creation behavior.

Consume RuntimeActivity and camelCase Core events, including closed-Team route cleanup. Own compaction and interruption labels and namespace display rows by kind and native id. Preserve card presentation, tool error priority and JSON formatting with structured payloads.
Render the new token.usage activity on the CoT card as the historical one-line Context/Token usage summary; formatting now lives only in this display layer.

patch.comment: Preserve newly sent pairing tokens after expiry and retire COT presentations when their serving parent route is released. Restore channel behavior coverage. Retire the displaced presentation after automatic provisioning commits over a concurrent manual bind, preserving same-Team and failed-commit behavior. Remove the unused internal default plugin wrapper. Share the post-commit bind presentation owner across manual and provisioned binding while retaining alternate receipt roots and anchor policy.
Restore a subtle sixth-level RESULT heading above the tool-result divider in Feishu COT cards.

Retire inherited Team presentation on an exact topic takeover and allow fresh inherited presentation after topic unbind, using committed routing facts without changing anchor provenance. Keep pairing credentials out of fresh and resend decision logs while preserving pairing actions and stored tokens.

On the `/teams` card, a topic binding's link now opens that topic in Feishu rather than the group it lives in. The link is built in the same shape as the `message_app_link` Feishu returns for a topic message. A group binding's link is unchanged and still opens the chat.
Bind fixed runtime context once and return persistence and cleanup operations to their owning services.

none.comment: Make the two hanging-resource-stream budget tests clock-deterministic so they no longer flake on congested CI runners.

Final pass (R53): widened OpenRound.threadId to `string | undefined` to match FeishuSentMessage.threadId under exactOptionalPropertyTypes, and dropped FeishuSession.toolSession()'s unused caller parameter (the R41 Collaboration-Space guard ended up threading through sendText's own options instead) along with its one call site. Both fixes make an already-uncompiled stage edit build; no behavior or published-API change.

Code organization refactor stage 1: wired the shared package-wide re-export ban (only src/index.ts may re-export another module) and a warn-only filename-convention lint rule. Lint config and inline eslint-disable comments only; no runtime or published-API change.

Code organization refactor stage 2a, item 1: updated to the tightened dreamux-types context contract (ChannelSessionCreateContext.logger/.state_root/.cache_root now required); deleted the now-dead console-fallback logger in provider.ts and collapsed the adjacent state_root guard into a single falsy check covering both the missing and empty-string cases. Internal-only; no runtime or published-API change.

Code organization refactor stage 3: added prettier --check to the package's lint script and reformatted src/tests/ to the shared repo-root config (R2). Whitespace/quote-style only; no runtime or published-API change.

Code organization refactor stage 9, item 8: deleted the failing 'the routing surface it does export owns only Feishu-local target/document concepts' case in tests/public-api.test.ts, per R43 -- the package's public barrel no longer exports a name called FeishuRouting. Test-only; no runtime or published-API change.

minor.comment: Remove the dead `FeishuBot.inviteMembers` pass-through and its test fakes. The method was added for the dispatcher-only `team.create_group` flow and has had no caller since that flow was retired in the #182 PR-8 cleanup; `FeishuBot` is a Dreamux-internal contract. The Feishu transport `createGroup`/`inviteMembers` wrappers and their exported types are intentionally kept.

The built-in Feishu Channel recognizes human-authored /stop, /teams, and /dissolve after ordinary inbound authorization. Commands reply directly without creating a model turn and touch no routing state, and /teams renders the current Running Team locator card. The /introduce acknowledgement is now in English.
Consume the canonical Team summary for provisioning and manual binding, and tighten the approved Card 2.0 route-notification layout.

COT tool rows now show what the call was: an argument code segment, then a RESULT label and divider, then the output, with a failure line inside the result area instead of ahead of the arguments. A call that named the items it was about still shows those pills alone, now including a failed one. A row the runtime labelled but named no action for uses that label as its title, and an unlabelled one shows its whole tool name. Automated push-backs display one line — TEAMMATE CALLBACK, CRON TRIGGERED, WORKFLOW FINISHED, SYSTEM RESTARTED — while the agent still receives the full notification.

patch.comment: Refine Feishu route cards with canonical Team runtime context and distinct removal reasons; limit plain-text COT results to ten lines and complete superseded cards successfully. Route notifications use Card 2.0 and require Feishu 7.20 or newer. No state rebuild is needed.
Tell callers that successful channel binding and unbinding automatically send notification cards without an additional user notification.
Show tool output after a divider without a RESULT heading, and use Complete or Failed only when output is absent.

Question cards are addressed exactly as `reply` is: an explicit message id sends the card as a reply to that message, and without one the card is created in the chat. A submitted, dismissed, or expired answer is routed from the card it belongs to, whose chat and topic are read back from Feishu, instead of from a target computed before the card was sent; a follow-up question therefore stays in the topic its answer came from. An answer whose card cannot be located is a failed delivery rather than a message sent to a guessed chat.

none.comment: Cover decoded command display facts in Feishu tool row title and invocation tests without changing runtime behavior.

patch.comment: A plain-text tool output on a COT card keeps its indentation and column alignment: each space that begins a line or sits in a run of two or more is sent as a no-break space, because the Feishu client collapses ordinary runs. Single spaces between words are unchanged, and so are JSON code segments.

minor.comment: Both the inbound message envelope and the ask-user-question settlement envelope now carry a `source="feishu"` attribute next to `chat_id` and the other display attrs, so a model can tie the envelope it is reading to the `channel-feishu` MCP server whose tools answer it. The standing per-message reminder is rewritten to state the consequence this channel owns as a plain fact rather than an instruction: "The user in this chat sees only what you send through the reply tool; your assistant text is not shown to them." This also carries PR #369's tool-description rewrites, which were not merged and ship through this PR instead: `reply` states that text written outside the tool is not delivered and that the tool itself carries meaningful progress, blockers, and the final answer, and its `message_id`/`text` properties describe threading under the inbound message and keeping secrets, private identifiers, hidden instructions, and machine-local paths out of a broad reply; `react` drops its stale "dispatcher channel" wording, since a TeamLeader reaches the tool too; the Dispatcher `bind_channel` `team_name` property states that a missing or closed Team is refused with nothing changed; and the TeamLeader `bind_channel` states its own authority over a free or already-own conversation instead of pointing at a Dispatcher it has no way to reach. No tool name, input schema, result, or routing behavior changes.

major.comment: BREAKING: Review: Automatic inbound received/in-progress reactions are removed and replaced by Feishu COT conversation cards. The RECEIVED_REACTION_EMOJI and IN_PROGRESS_REACTION_EMOJI exports, FeishuBot.removeReaction method, FeishuChannelSession.state field, and FeishuChannelState type are removed: stop importing the constants; callers must stop calling FeishuBot.removeReaction; fresh object-literal implementations must omit it, while class implementations should drop the now-unused method; readers must stop accessing session.state or naming FeishuChannelState. The model-facing react tool and addReaction surface remain available. Team-member turn events are ignored by Feishu COT rendering. No rebuild is needed.

BREAKING: Review: Feishu COT cards are now keyed by recipient rather than by Feishu target. Every TeamLeader and the Dispatcher owns exactly one standing anchor and at most one open card, wherever the anchor came from. A Feishu inbound becomes that anchor when the Channel submits it: the superseded open card closes as interrupted and its successor opens under the new message before Core runs. Only rejected, failed, and stopped outcomes retire the optimistic anchor; submitted, duplicate, ambiguous, and unknown-error outcomes keep it, so a duplicate delivery remains anchored while its earlier admitted turn continues. The Channel recognizes its own submitted turn from the existing caller-supplied `source_id` and hides that turn's already-visible user body once; every other producer's body displays normally. A card closes only when the runtime reports the end of its one native turn (completed closes as done; failed or interrupted closes as interrupted); that fact closes an already open card and never opens one, so it is ignored when no card is open. `teammate.turn.settled` no longer closes, reopens, or re-anchors anything. A card create or append the platform refuses abandons only that card: the standing anchor survives, and the next opening activity tries to open a card there again. A Reply is outbound only and never creates, replaces, or retires an anchor. A visible Team bind card may initialize a TeamLeader that has no standing anchor and never replaces an existing one; the Dispatcher has no installation or restart anchor. A tool result that arrives after an anchor replacement may be omitted. Anchors and cards live only in the live session's memory and are lost on restart by design, with no replay or backfill. The package's public export surface is unchanged; the target-keyed and dispatcher-scoped COT presentation modules this replaces were always internal. No transport, configuration, persisted state, or path shape changed and no rebuild is required.

BREAKING: Review: A Feishu inbound now becomes the selected Dispatcher or TeamLeader's COT anchor immediately when the Channel submits it, interrupting the prior card and opening the successor receipt before Core runs. Only rejected, failed, and stopped outcomes retire that optimistic anchor; submitted, duplicate, ambiguous, and unknown-error outcomes keep it, while unsubmitted means no Core submission anchor was taken before Dispatcher fallback. In particular, a duplicate delivery keeps the repeated message anchored while its already-admitted turn continues. The Channel recognizes its own turn from the existing caller-supplied `source_id` echoed on `teammate.turn.submitted` and hides that turn's already-visible user body exactly once; other producers' bodies remain visible. Correlation is bounded and released. Body-text matching is deliberately not used because path, secret, or truncation sanitization can change projected text and silently defeat suppression. No config or persisted-state shape changes, and no rebuild is needed.

BREAKING: creating a Feishu channel session without an explicit state root now fails instead of falling back to the process working directory. Previously an omitted `state_root` silently wrote the session's durable routing state — bindings, spaces, dispatcher access — into whatever directory the process happened to start in, a silent-data-corruption footgun that surfaced only later as state that had disappeared. `createSession` now throws immediately with a message naming the requirement. The published context type still marks `state_root` optional, so this is a runtime-behavior break rather than a type break. Dreamux hosts always inject a per-dispatcher state root and are unaffected; an embedder that relied on the implicit fallback must now provide `state_root` explicitly. No config, state, or path shape changed and no rebuild is required.

BREAKING: Rebuild: recreate every Feishu binding and collaboration-space policy with this Channel's own MCP tools after upgrading; Core's previous binding state is not migrated. This Channel now owns routing end to end: a durable per-channel binding document under the dispatcher state dir, direct and hierarchical target resolution, stale-binding cleanup, and automatic collaboration-space provisioning composed from ordinary `team.create` and `team.submit` Commands. Its MCP catalog is caller-scoped and replaces the removed Core tools: `bind_channel`, `unbind_channel`, and `list_bindings` for the Dispatcher, self-scoped `bind_channel`/`unbind_channel` for a TeamLeader, and the four collaboration-space policy tools for the Dispatcher; there is no `transfer_back` (rebind with a different `team_name`). A bind is refused when the named Team is missing or closed, and it mutates no routing state. Inbound submissions now pass display attributes and faithful body text through `team.submit` and Core renders the channel envelope.

BREAKING: Review: watch one COT card end-to-end after upgrading, including one input that fails before a runtime accepts it — that card now reads 任务失败 instead of 已中断. No config, state, cache, or path shape changed and no rebuild is needed. The session now subscribes to `teammate.input` and `teammate.activity` instead of the five deleted turn-scoped kinds, and recognizes its own inbound body by comparing `source_id` against the ids this session issued rather than through a two-hop turn correlation. A card's one terminal is a `turn.ended` activity, which prints its reason on the card before ending it. That terminal is now three-valued across two AG-UI events: a `completed` end sends `RUN_FINISHED done`, an `interrupted` end and every lifecycle interrupt send `RUN_FINISHED interrupted`, and a `failed` end sends `RUN_ERROR`, which is what the Feishu client renders as 任务失败 — a submission no runtime accepted used to end the card as 已中断. Open tool calls are keyed on the runtime's call id alone.

minor.comment: COT tool rows show what the runtime said about the call: the row title is the runtime's summary (with a verb for read/list/search/edit rows and the tool name for rows without an action), the row carries the documented built-in icon for its action (bash/read/write/search), raw JSON arguments are no longer written into any row (a call nothing could label, such as an MCP tool, shows its name behind the icon-library token app-default_outlined with its arguments hidden), and the expanded result shows the invocation as a code segment before the output. A read or edit that succeeded expands to the files it touched as pills (a +N pill stands for those past the pill budget) and nothing else; a failed one keeps its diff and output after the pills. Result code segments now use the documented code field. An output that parses as a JSON object or array is pretty-printed in a json code segment; any other output is plain text (previously every output was a text code segment, with a one-line output under 120 bytes shown inline). Every card string is now cut only where it would exceed Feishu's 4,096-byte per-event content limit, with the truncation marker; the former 512-byte invocation and title soft caps and the 1,024-byte output soft cap are gone. The card's own words are now English: row verbs (Read/List/Search/Edit), the Completed/Failed status lines, and the truncation marker. The Channel no longer composes titles or result text for Dreamux's teammate tools (spawn, send, close, workflow_run) from their arguments, nor for its own reply, react and list_chat_bots tools; all of those show as unlabelled tool rows behind the generic app icon.

Render the COT card's opening label with a glyph Feishu shows as text. The previous character is in the Unicode emoji set, so Feishu replaced it with a coloured emoji tile; the replacement is a dingbat with no emoji presentation. Labels and behaviour are otherwise unchanged.

Open a Feishu COT card with one of five flavour labels chosen independently per card, replacing the fixed line that said processing had started. That line was written before Core was called, so it asserted an admission the Channel could not yet know; an ambiguous submission may never reach the runtime. The opening line now states nothing about admission or progress. Cards are append-only, so the label is picked once when the card opens and does not animate. This is an intentional operator-visible presentation change to a deliberately tuned surface.

Add the `ask_user_question` MCP tool: the model sends a Feishu decision card (1-4 single-select questions, each option carrying a label and a description) and the tool returns as soon as the card is sent. The answer is not awaited — a click settles the round server-side and the result arrives as an ordinary inbound message, so a user may take as long as they like. An optional `message_id` addresses the card under the message the question came out of, the way a reply is addressed. A round closes itself before Feishu stops accepting clicks on the card and tells the model no answer came.

patch.comment: Derive the automatic-provisioning `team.create` request id from the inbound Feishu message that triggered it, instead of minting a fresh UUID per attempt. A message the platform redelivers now replays the same request id, so Core's idempotency answers with the Team the first attempt created rather than provisioning a duplicate for one conversation; when the first attempt died between creating the Team and installing the route, the replay reports the existing Team and the run finishes the binding, recovering instead of duplicating. Request identity is scoped to the message rather than the topic on purpose: a new message after a Team is dissolved mints a new id, so the same topic provisions a fresh Team normally. A different message arriving after a partial failure still creates a second Team, a window left undefended by design, and a redelivered id whose space policy changed in between fails loud as an idempotency conflict, reporting the message unsubmitted so it falls back to the Dispatcher Agent.

none.comment: Documentation-only: update knowledge-base citation paths in the package README after the .agents reorganization; no package behavior or version change.

major.comment: BREAKING: Review: before deploying, inspect every existing non-empty group.allow_chats entry under both group.policy=allowlist and group.policy=follow-user; keep only groups whose human membership should be trusted and whose passive known-bot observation should remain enabled. Previously, follow-user ignored allow_chats for ordinary human delivery, while allowlist still applied dm_policy and allow_users after the chat check. Now either non-block policy trusts every exactly classified human in a listed chat after the global mention gate. access.json remains V3 and needs no rebuild; the new authorization meaning takes effect in place when the new server starts. The package-root gate input remains unchanged, and callers must classify an exact human before passing is_bot_sender=false.

BREAKING: Publish complete Feishu MCP tool metadata and closed input/output schemas. Successful reply and react calls now return direct canonical message_ids and reaction_id objects, while live and sessionless list_chat_bots calls return the same direct chat_id, known, and trusted result.

BREAKING: Review: Channel contract consumers must use status-only delivery results, treat admission-ambiguous as terminal and non-replayed, and stop subscribing to the removed turn.submitted and turn.settled events. Feishu delivery no longer exposes Dreamux Turn IDs. No rebuild is required: Feishu config, access state, bindings, and transport state formats are unchanged.

minor.comment: Expose caller-owned cancellation for interactive card sends and document timeout outcomes as remotely unknown.

patch.comment: Send independent best-effort Feishu cards for binding route and collaboration-space transitions, retrying a failed or timed-out attempt once in memory.

major.comment: BREAKING: The public Feishu formatter now returns structured Channel-owned content/ref XML, renders downloaded inline attachments as path-only elements and non-downloaded attachments as status/key-only elements, and renders create time as process-local unpadded time instead of UTC ISO. Accepted unnamed human turns may await a best-effort contact lookup for up to two seconds. Consumers that parse formatter body text, attachment attributes, or ISO timestamps must adopt the new contracts.

patch.comment: Make Feishu channel acknowledgements conditional so immediately answerable requests receive a single direct reply.

minor.comment: Add backwards-compatible Feishu topic-group projection, fail-safe chat-mode verification, and exact topic reply authorization.
Preserve enclosing group bindings for non-collaboration topic groups and expose inbound thread_id to the model-visible channel envelope.

major.comment: BREAKING: Remove the root-exported createFakeFeishuBot test helper and FakeFeishuBot type. Tests must provide package-local FeishuBot doubles; runtime behavior and persisted state are unchanged.

minor.comment: BREAKING: Stop authoring channel MCP descriptors in the Feishu provider. The package now exposes only the static Feishu tool catalog plus reply/react/list_chat_bots handlers; Dreamux core renders the channel-mcp descriptor, admin socket, caller, team, and leader routing args.

patch.comment: Clear the optimistic Feishu inbound received reaction when core submission throws before delivery, preventing a stale received marker on failed inbound turns.

major.comment: BREAKING: remove the Feishu `access` MCP tool and make Owner-only interactive cards the only pairing approval surface. The channel now sends an interactive approval card for pending pairing requests, rejects non-Owner clicks with a toast-only response, and lets the App Owner approve through the card callback. The callback reuses the internal approve-by-token helper, then returns Feishu's raw-card callback response for the green success state. Existing callers must stop invoking the removed `access` tool; inspect or revoke pending entries by editing access.json directly.

minor.comment: The Feishu channel session now exposes provider-owned target resolution: `FeishuChannelSession.resolveTarget(meta)` maps a `{ chat_id, chat_type }` selector to a neutral `ChannelTarget` (group chats are bindable, P2P chats are not; `target_key` is the chat id). This is the provider half of Dreamux core's binding store v2 + `(channel_id, target_key)` routing (issue #209). Additive — existing session behavior is unchanged; the neutral `ChannelSession` wrapper now delegates to this method instead of duplicating the mapping.

Promote @excitedjs/feishu-channel from scaffold to the publishable built-in Feishu ChannelProvider package (alias builtin:feishu, issue #209 slice 5). It now owns the live Feishu channel session, access/trust behavior, inbound normalization, attachment handling, target resolution, MCP descriptor, and provider tool backing (`reply` / `react` / `list_chat_bots`), implementing the neutral @excitedjs/dreamux-types ChannelProvider/ChannelSession contract on top of @excitedjs/feishu-transport. Depends on @excitedjs/dreamux-types + @excitedjs/feishu-transport only — never on @excitedjs/dreamux core. The host supplies provider-validated config plus neutral state/cache roots through the session context; core keeps only routing, binding state, authorization, and the generic admin conduit.

The Feishu channel provider's `readConfig` is now the config-validation authority for `builtin:feishu` (issue #209 multi-channel config): Dreamux core registers this provider and calls `readConfig` at config load instead of validating Feishu fields itself. `readConfig` now fails loud on an empty/whitespace `app_id` or `app_secret` (the bot secret is config-sourced, so this preserves the host's previous config-load fail-loud) and on unknown config keys. Parsing of a valid `{ app_id, app_secret }` into `{ appId, appSecret }` is unchanged.

The built-in Feishu Channel provider now owns onboarding prompts for bot app id and app secret and exposes a provider diagnostic capability. Dreamux core records the returned raw config and drives the channel through the shared provider diagnostic contract instead of hardcoding Feishu fields in onboard or doctor.

patch.comment: The Feishu provider's `mcpServerDescriptor` now targets Dreamux core's generic channel-tool shim: descriptor args change from `feishu-mcp ...` to `channel-mcp --provider builtin:feishu --channel-id <id> --dispatcher <id> ...`. The MCP server name (`feishu`) and provider tool surface (`reply` / `react` / `list_chat_bots`) are unchanged. The shim serves the provider's static `tools/list` metadata and forwards `tools/call` to the neutral `channel.invoke_tool` admin method; binding remains on the Team MCP and is not a channel-tool responsibility. Rebuild: none required — descriptors are regenerated at every dispatcher boot, never persisted.

Type the package's default factory export against the published `ChannelProviderFactory` contract and use the kind-narrowed `ChannelProviderDescriptor` for the builtin descriptor (issue #209 types-API audit). No runtime behavior change.
Adopt the shared @excitedjs/eslint-config flat config and the synchronous-blocking-IO lint gate (issue #85); no runtime change

major.comment:
BREAKING: Replace the v2 access gate (inline `FeishuChannelSession.onMessage` branches + transport `policy/gate.ts` + `contract/access-store.ts`) with the access-gate-v3 pairing-code mechanism. The persisted dispatcher access state now uses `DispatcherAccessStateV3` (`version: 3`) and the loader fails loud when an older version is detected — no silent migration.

Rebuild: Your existing v2 dispatcher access file (usually `<dispatcher-state-root>/feishu/dispatcher_access.json`) is **not** deleted automatically — the v3 loader crashes loudly on v2. Preserve your existing access list before upgrading, then create a fresh state file. From your current v2 file, copy the following fields verbatim into a new file named `access.json` in the same directory: `allow_users`, `group.allow_chats`, `group.require_mention`, then add `"version": 3`, `"dm_policy": "allowlist"`, `"pending": {}`, `"known_banned_senders": []`. A sibling `chat-bots.json` will be created on first session start from the in-memory chat-bots ledger; the former v2 inline chat_bots entries are NOT ported automatically (it is OK to lose them; the channel rebuilds the ledger live from the first few bot encounters — no data loss for pairing or allowlist behavior).

Highlights:
- 22-line table-driven `dreamuxFeishuGate()` pure function covering (DM × 5 policies × pairing-resend) + (group × 5 policies × mention gate × pairing-resend × trusted-bot + bot-self) branches.
- `require_mention: true` default (product decision).
- Follow-user strangers in a group who @-mention the bot now receive a pairing code (product decision — no cooldown / default-drop switch).
- Per-kind pending-pairing quota: `MAX_PENDING_PER_KIND = 10`, independent for DM vs group, with expired entries excluded before the count.
- TTL double guard: `pruneExpiredPending` at gate entry + inline `expires_at > now` check inside `findExistingPendingByKey`.
- Pairing-code prompt rendered with the bot display name and a 6-hex code; resends use the same code.
- LOCK-SEND-LOCK pattern on the pairing path: gate + first save under `AsyncMutex`, then `sendText` outside the lock, then re-enter the lock to read the latest state and only persist the fresh pending entry when the send succeeded and no earlier concurrent entry already covers the same (kind, key) slot.
- `approvePairingByCode` is idempotent on membership (duplicate approve → reported as `duplicate: true`; pending key is always removed).
- MCP `access` tool now has a real handler; `reply` / `react` / `list_chat_bots` / `access` centralized in `tools/registry.ts`.
- Atomic write for the access-state file (tmpfile + rename, mode `0o600`; directory created at mode `0o700`).
- `TRUST_DOMAIN_WARNING` exported from the barrel index for operator-facing UIs.
- Transport hard boundary: `@excitedjs/feishu-transport` no longer ships any access-control or persistence logic.
